title: Tax Information Release No. 2025-03: Withholding of Taxes on Income of Nonresident Partners and Beneficiaries

TAX INFORMATION RELEASE NO. 2025-03
RE: Withholding of Taxes on Income of Nonresident Partners and Beneficiaries
The purpose of this Tax Information Release (TIR) is to provide guidance on section 235-
64.2, Hawaii Revised Statutes (HRS), which requires partnerships, estates, and trusts withhold an
amount equal to the highest marginal tax rate applicable to a nonresident taxpayer, multiplied by
the taxpayer’s distributive share of income attributable to Hawaiʻi.
Partnerships, Estates, and Trusts Subject to Withholding Requirement
Withholding under section 235-64.2, HRS, applies to partnerships, estates, and trusts.
Publicly traded partnerships, as defined by section 7704(b) of the Internal Revenue Code,
are not subject to withholding, but must file an annual information return reporting the name,
address, and taxpayer identification number of each unit holder with income sourced to Hawaiʻi.
Partnerships that elect pass-through entity (PTE) taxation under section 235-51.5, HRS,
are not subject to withholding under section 235-64.2, HRS, provided the partnership properly
elects PTE taxation and makes the required PTE payment.
Nonresident Taxpayers Subject to Withholding
Partnerships, estates, and trusts are required to withhold tax on behalf of nonresident
individual partners and beneficiaries. Withholding is not required on behalf of partners or
beneficiaries that are corporations, pass-through entities, estates, trusts, or other entities.
Withholding Calculation
The amount of withholding shall equal 11 percent of the nonresident individual taxpayer's
distributive share of income attributable to Hawaiʻi. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the
Department of Taxation will not challenge the withholding of any amount reasonably determined
by a partnership, estate, or trust that approximates the nonresident individual's actual tax liability
(e.g., calculations based on the capital gains rate or exclusion of amounts not subject to tax).
Taxpayers must keep records supporting their calculation of the withholding amount.
